### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c33707933a57071b57bef9cd488f63c2c06d951f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b0db490ea7170b95b6b6affa47faf1f0706e788b`

Round 1 · isolated at-tier contract reviewer spawned by the `domain:spec` seat-3 PM (seat post #18883), because the lane owes this record on every round it delivers, `Clause-②: yes` or `no`. Head asserted with `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/19434/head` at the start (20:40Z) and again immediately before this post (21:17:19Z); both read the sha above. Measured in a detached worktree at that head (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exit 0), every exit captured before any pipe. The shared checkout was not edited, stashed or moved.

### ① Derived judgments

**Z1 — `Clause-②: no` is correct, judged rather than inherited.** The diff is 3 files (+638/−1): a new `scripts/check-dts-references.mjs`, one `&&` link in `packages/spec` `scripts.build`, one unconditional `--self-test` step in `lint.yml`. Both manifests parsed: `files[]`, `exports` (19 keys), `types`/`main` are equal between the merge-base a0e62e69 and the head; only `scripts.build` differs. No Zod schema, no authorable key, no export, no CLI flag, no new env var (`OS_SKIP_DTS` is the sibling guard's existing stand-down; measured: exit 0 with the stand-down line). The guard's inputs are the package's own manifest and its emitted `dist/**` declarations — build output, nothing a user authors — and its only effect is a non-zero exit of ObjectStack's own build. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:api-surface` after a real build: exit 0, "public API surface + factory signatures unchanged". Nothing a user may author is widened or narrowed, so no arm applies and `no` stands.

**Z2 — the seam, re-derived, not re-read.**
- A (tsup's own emission record), ruled out — reproduced. tsup 8.5.1 as resolved from `packages/spec`: `metafile` occurs 0 times in `dist/rollup.js`; lit control on the same file and grep: 16 lines `rollup` / 45 lines `dts` (the dev's counts are `grep -c` line counts, reproduced exactly; 28 / 57 as occurrences). Positive control on the JS side: `metafile` 10 times in `dist/index.js` (`metafile: result.metafile`). The zero is an absence the instrument can see.
- B (closure of the emitted declarations' own relative references), chosen — reproduced. A scratch probe importing `walkDeclarationGraph` and `declaredDeclarationPaths` and walking every declaration under `dist/**`: 34 roots, closure 124, declaration files on disk 124, **orphans 0**, reached-but-absent 0, 366 relative references all resolved, 116 bare, positions 318 import / 164 export / 0 of the other four. On this package the closure equals the emission; the load-bearing zero holds.
- C (`check-dev-prereqs --stamp` as owner), ruled out — population reproduced: 68 build scripts run `check-dts-emitted.mjs`; exactly 4 also run `--stamp` (`AMPLIFIERS`: spec, core, plugin-auth, organizations); 12 of the 68 declare more than one entry STEM (the dev's number; counted per declared declaration PATH it is 33, because most entries ship `.d.ts` and `.d.mts`). Of the 4 stamped, organizations has one stem and is not chunk-capable; 9 of the 12 chunk-capable packages are not stamped. Subject confirmed by the ablation below: with 2 chunks missing the stamp still reads `match`, because it digests INPUTS.

**Z3 — the guard fires; both legs re-run on my own build (62 `.d.ts`; sha256 of every moved file recorded first).**
RED — `dist/view.zod-CIU5lVgU.d.ts` and `dist/object.zod-ThXvwL_J.d.ts` moved aside (count 62 to 60): `check-dts-emitted.mjs` exit **0** "34/34 declared declaration file(s) present"; `distIsStale()` **false**, `declarationStamp()` **match**; `check-dts-references.mjs` exit **1**, 19 findings naming every referrer across the 4 missing targets (the `./` and `../` spellings of both chunks); `check:api-surface` exit **1**, "233 breaking (removed/narrowed), 227 added", 229 removal lines — the dev's re-taken numbers, reproduced exactly.
LIT CONTROL — one DECLARED entry (`dist/meta-spelling/index.d.ts`) moved aside instead: `check-dts-emitted.mjs` exit **1** naming it (the new guard also exits 1, naming it as a missing root attributed to `package.json`). One zero and one hit on the same instrument: the chunk-level zero is a coverage gap, not a dead instrument.
Restores: `sha256sum -c` OK on all three files, count back to 62; GREEN: emitted 0 / references 0 / api-surface 0.
`--self-test`: exit 0. An instrumented copy in scratch reads batteries 7 / 11 / 2 = 20 cases over the pinned floor of 3 batteries. Two negative controls on copies: deleting one prose case reds the floor (exit 1, "registered 1 case(s), below its pinned floor of 2"); an early `return` before the verdict trips the handshake (exit 1, "returned without reaching its verdict"). A truncated declaration is refused by `ts-parse`, which names the file and exits **3** — non-zero, so the build fails on that shape too.

**Z4 — wiring.** The new link sits between `check-dts-emitted.mjs` and `check-dev-prereqs.mjs --stamp`, and the stamp is still the LAST `&&` link (`stampStepOrderProblem` accepts the spelling; `check:dev-prereqs --self-test` exit 0, 19 batteries / 76 cases). Chain probe on the RED tree, running the build's `&&` tail from `packages/spec`: exit **1**, the stamp step never ran (0 lines from it), `dist/.build-input-hash-dts` mtime untouched; GREEN control on the restored tree: exit 0 and the stamp is rewritten. A failure in the new step fails the build and withholds the stamp — nothing swallows it. Direct `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` at the head: exit 0 in 2m48s with the guard's own line printed inside the build ("124 declaration file(s) reachable from 34 declared entry point(s); 366/366"). On the cache argument: turbo's `build` task declares no `inputs`, so `package.json` is hashed — `spec#build` hashes eb984dc2… at the merge-base and ebae4bcb… at the head, with the `scripts.build` line the only `packages/spec` diff between them — so CI's Build Core (success on this head) cannot have replayed main's entry for spec. My own `pnpm build` (72/72) was a LOCAL cache hit of the dev's run through the shared `.turbo/cache`, and its replayed log carries the guard's success line: an entry that exists only because that build exited 0, which is exactly the property the placement relies on.
The `lint.yml` step, parsed from YAML rather than read: index 19 of 183 in the `lint` job (`Lint & Repo Gates`, a required context), name intact, no `if:`, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (index 5); root devDeps carry `typescript`. I agree the `--self-test`-only step is the right instrument there: a healthy tree is green by construction, so only the self-test's partial-emission fixture exercises the RED direction in CI, and the step is unconditional. eslint over the new script: exit 0.

**Z5 — radius.** `git diff a0e62e69..b0db490e -- scripts/pm/check-regen-pending.mjs scripts/check-dts-emitted.mjs scripts/check-dev-prereqs.mjs` is 0 bytes, and the whole diff is the 3 files above, so `distIsStale()`, its legs, its acceptance set, `buildInputHash` and `check-dts-emitted.mjs`'s declared scope are byte-unchanged by construction. `declaredDeclarationPaths` is an existing export that `check-dts-closure.mjs` already imports; this adds a third importer and changes nothing in it. #19086 is open, `needs-user-decision`, unassigned, last updated 16:35Z (before this PR opened), and nothing here touches its subject — not pre-empted.

**Z6 — gates.** Re-derived from the head tree with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: **105** commands (byte-identical whether the change set is read from git or named as the 3 explicit paths; a derivation from a tree at `origin/main` bed71880 prints 103 — the two missing are this PR's own new self-test and `bare-root-worklist --self-test`, which is placed by the new gate script's existence, so the 105 is the right list). Every command run after `pnpm build` (72/72) with its true exit captured before any pipe and recorded beside the command: **104 exit 0, 1 exit 3** (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`: its positive-control fixture is pinned to 621a4876, outside this clone's shallow horizon at ae8edd2c — PREREQUISITE NOT MET, not a red; same reading as the dev). `--ran` reconciliation: exit 0, "105 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 104 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (1 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)". `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` exit 0 at its real budget (856 s) — I agree with the dev's disclosure that its 124 at a 200 s cap was a timeout, not a red; the three families that needed the built closure read exit 0 here because the closure was built first. Sweep 20:51–21:16Z.
CI on this head, per check name, newest run wins, read 21:17:20Z: 36 check names, **30 success / 6 skipped / 0 in progress / 0 failure**. Every gate-carrying context is `success`: Lint & Repo Gates (which ran the new self-test step), Build Core (which ran `packages/spec`'s build with the new link), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test Core (aggregate plus 6/6 shards), Dogfood Regression Gate (aggregate plus 3/3 shards), and the 4 Type Check jobs (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger). Skipped by their own filters: Auto Label, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in) — `Check Changeset` was `failure` at 20:34:19Z on its first run and `skipped` on the newest run after the label; newest-run-wins, so no red stands on this head.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` — agreed (the label was applied by the seat at 20:35:22Z after `Check Changeset` reddened at 20:34Z; the newest run of that check on this head is `skipped`). Route 0 cannot apply: the diff has zero `.changeset` rows, so no pending note of anybody else's was changed. Route 2 is the gate's own preferred route for a diff that releases nothing, and it releases nothing: grep over everything `files[]` ships (`dist json-schema liveness prompts llms.txt README.md src/**/*.zod.ts CHANGELOG.md api-surface spec-changes.json`, all present after the build) for `check-dts-references`: **0** files; positive control `defineStack` on the same trees: 158 files (the dev read 256 — the control's resolution differs, the zero does not). The one published byte that moves is the `scripts.build` string inside `package.json`, which no consumer executes. Precedent: PR #12076, which adopted the sibling `check-dts-emitted.mjs` into a build script, landed with `skip-changeset` and 0 `.changeset` rows. No level, no arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No boundary moves: the guard reads `dist/**` and the manifest and exits the build; no user-facing acceptance changes in either direction.
- Observation, not a blocker: `referenceCandidates` sends an unrecognised extension (a `.json` specifier, say) to the extensionless branch, which would red on a legitimate `resolveJsonModule` declaration; every path tried is printed so it is diagnosable, and no such reference exists in this tree (366/366).
- Rollout to the other 67 adopters is measured-safe here too — the guard run from each of the 68 adopter directories on the built closure: 68/68 exit 0 — and it is correctly left for the seat to file rather than taken in this card.

**NOT MEASURED:** (1) `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` — exit 3 on the shallow clone, its positive control unreachable; environment, unaffected by any path here. (2) CI logs of Build Core and the first `Check Changeset` run were not read in full — the proxy refuses the Azure blob host that serves job logs (CONNECT 403); the `Check Changeset` failure text was read through the MCP tail ("This PR adds no changeset … apply the 'skip-changeset' label"), and the Build Core verdict is read from the check-run conclusion plus the fact that turbo hashed `spec#build` freshly on this head. (3) A real interrupted DTS pass was not produced — the partial state was constructed by moving files aside, as on the card; frequency remains unmeasured. (4) The dev's 68/68 adopter sweep was reproduced on my build (68/68 exit 0) but adoption itself is out of scope and not judged.
